..
A narrow line of showers is moving towards Guam this evening,
however, the radar loop suggests that this line is diminishing as it
approaches. Isolated showers are expected through the remainder of 
the week. Enjoy the sunny days, but try to start conserving water as 
we are transitioning into the dry season.

Marine...
Gentle to moderate easterly trade winds will decrease to light to
gentle as early as Tuesday night. Winds may build up to moderate 
for the weekend. Combined seas of 5 to 7 ft will build to 6 to 8 
feet by late week due to building northwest to north swell, 
emanating from distant Typhoon Cempaka.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Cempaka (31W) has strengthened, with maximum sustained winds
at 85 mph. It's currently located 410 miles west-southwest of Iwo To
based on the latest visible imagery. Cempaka is forecast to intensify
through tonight, while making an east-northeast turn as it slows its
forward speed somewhat through Tuesday. Typhoon force winds extend 
outward from the center up to 25 miles. Tropical storm force winds 
extend outward from the center up to 100 miles.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main feature of interest is a Near-Equatorial Trough that
stretches from the southern edge of Pohnpei's coastal waters to just
northeast of Kosrae, to Makin in the southern RMI (Republic of the
Marshall Islands). This feature continues to be a focus for shower
and thunderstorm development due to some slight moisture pooling and
modest, but sufficient, surface convergence. This has allowed
scattered showers to affect Kosrae through the day, and this looks to
continue through Tuesday. Pohnpei and Majuro remain far enough
removed from this feature, so just isolated showers are expected
through tomorrow. Then, the NET is forecast to settle south and exit
the area as it crosses the equator. With the lack of any features to
focus any convective development, isolated showers area-wide look to
persist into the weekend for Pohnpei and Kosrae. For Majuro, a
tropical disturbance passing by to the north may allow sufficient
convergence along the tail of a developing trough to allow for
scattered showers to develop Thursday into Friday.

Seas of 4 to 6 feet will continue through the week for Pohnpei and
Kosrae. At Majuro, seas will be in the 5 to 7 foot range through the
middle of the week, before decreasing a foot or so towards the
weekend. Winds will be light to gentle area-wide.

Western Micronesia...
A drier ridging pattern has moved in across Yap and Palau, behind 
the surface trough to the west which extends southward along 130E. 
Satellite imagery late this afternoon shows isolated showers moving 
southwest across the area, with upper-level cloud debris streaming 
over southern Yap waters from earlier thunderstorms this morning. The
trough west of Palau will linger near the southern Philippines for 
the next day or two while a weak surface ridge remains in place over 
Palau and Yap. This ridge will diminish Tuesday, allowing a broad 
circulation southwest of Chuuk to shift westward into the area, 
likely as a large open surface trough. Convergence will build along 
the northern edge of this trough, leading to scattered showers for 
Palau around Tuesday night. For the latter half of the week, a fairly
dry trade-wind regime is expected. However, current model guidance 
shows an increase in showers over Palau around Friday night, along 
the edge of a broad trade-wind convergence boundary that looks to 
develop across much of western and central Micronesia.

An area of trade-wind convergence is shifting northward across Chuuk,
associated with a broad circulation over southeast Yap State and the
extensive monsoon-like trough connected to it. Although latest 
satellite shows Chuuk Lagoon is currently between bands of showers 
to the north and south this evening, model guidance points to 
scattered showers developing overnight, before a drier pattern 
resumes on Tuesday.

Altimetry and Babeldaob buoy data show combined seas remain between 
4 to 6 feet across the region, mainly comprised of a northeast trade 
swell. Around Tuesday night, an elevated long-period north swell will
move into the region, emanating from distant Typhoon Cempaka. Then, a
stronger pulse of north swell looks to arrive around Thursday night
from distant systems farther north. These elevated, longer-period
north swells will increase seas by several feet for Palau and Yap by
the end of the week, and produce elevated surf along north-facing 
reefs. Surf may become hazardous along north reefs of Yap around 
Friday night into the weekend, and potentially for Palau around 
Saturday night.
